namingPrinciple: A concrete place plus an evocative modifier; no character ownership needed. Locale is a design-cycle label, not a new rules subtype. The ten cards remain ordinary common tapped dual lands.

lands.name: Homeward Harbor
lands.story: A sheltered Mediterranean harbor: a place of refuge and the promise of homecoming.
lands.artNote: Use the broad bay and island silhouette. The Knip composition includes later Roman ruins and a church: an evocative landscape, not an archaeological reconstruction of Ithaca.

lands.name: Mistbound Crossing
lands.story: A dark crossing toward the shore of the dead, recalling the journey to the shades.
lands.artNote: The existing verified Isle of the Dead is landscape-led: preserve the dark water, cypress mass and narrow landing.

lands.name: Great Hall
lands.story: The great hall as a place of feasting, rivalry, appetite and mounting violence.
lands.artNote: Lead with the colonnaded interior, not a named character. Later classical architectural fantasy; keep the room's depth and columns legible.

lands.name: Rugged Headland
lands.story: A wild rocky headland on the voyagers' route: powerful surf and ungoverned nature.
lands.artNote: Northeaster provides rocks, surf and sky without a modern ship. A nonliteral coastal analogue, not a claimed Greek location.

lands.name: Olive Pasture
lands.story: Olive-covered grazing country where the household's herds and ordinary work endure.
lands.artNote: Keep the olive grove and open ground dominant; no herdsman's name is required for the place to read.

lands.name: Silent Courtyard
lands.story: A quiet stone courtyard holding the memory of a household and those absent from it.
lands.artNote: Architectural space and empty thresholds, rather than a portrait of the waiting queen. Later Roman capriccio is an evocative substitute, explicitly not Bronze Age evidence.

lands.name: Windswept Isle
lands.story: An exposed island of sea wind, changing weather and uncertain passage.
lands.artNote: Use Moret's complete island-and-coast composition for geographical readability; Gathering Storm supplies the stronger wind-and-sky alternate. Neither requires Aeolus to appear.

lands.name: Asphodel Meadow
lands.story: The dim meadows beyond the crossing to the shades, where life and death share the same ground.
lands.artNote: Use the moonlit landscape as atmosphere rather than a literal botanical depiction of asphodel. No portrait or scene of named dead heroes is required.

lands.name: Laurel Grounds
lands.story: Open grounds for contests, communal games and the honor of athletic victory.
lands.artNote: Arcadian open ground and a ruined monument provide an environmental view. An imaginative locale, not a claim that the painting depicts the Phaeacian games.

lands.name: Palmshade Cove
lands.story: A lush sheltered cove of shade, warm water and enticing isolation.
lands.artNote: Tropical Coastal Landscape is a scenic analogue for the enchanted-island mood, not a literal map of Ogygia. Preserve the full coast and vegetation, not an invented portrait of Calypso.

artworks.title: Palace or Villa Interior, Colonnaded Hall
artworks.medium: Pen and brown ink, gray wash over black chalk
artworks.tags: Great Hall; Silent Courtyard; hall; colonnade; palace interior; architectural landscape
artworks.cropNotes: Keep the axial depth and complete column rhythm. Later classical architectural fantasy, not an exact ancient Greek megaron.

artworks.title: Tropical Coastal Landscape
artworks.tags: Tropical Cove; Palmshade Cove; tropical coast; landscape; sheltered shore
artworks.cropNotes: Keep the coast and vegetation dominant. A tropical scenic analogue for an enchanted island, not a literal Greek location.

artworks.title: Northeaster
artworks.tags: Rugged Headland; Windswept Isle; Windy Island; storm; surf; rocks; landscape
artworks.cropNotes: Rocks and breaking surf remain the subjects; no modern vessel to hide. Later landscape analogy, not Greek topography.

artworks.title: The Gulf of Naples with the Island of Ischia in the Distance
artworks.tags: Homeward Harbor; Windswept Isle; harbor; Mediterranean; island; landscape; ruins
artworks.candidateCards: Homeward Harbor; Windswept Isle; Palmshade Cove
artworks.cropNotes: A composite Italian vista with Roman monuments and a church. Prefer the bay and island silhouette; flag later architecture rather than pretending Bronze Age accuracy.

artworks.title: Gathering Storm on Long Island Sound
artworks.tags: Windy Island; Windswept Isle; storm; wind; coast; pines; landscape
artworks.cropNotes: Wind-shaped trees and threatening sky are an alternate mood for the exposed island. Later American coast used as an evocative landscape.

artworks.title: Landscape with herdsmen and cattle
artworks.tags: Olive Pasture; grazing; meadow; herds; landscape
artworks.cropNotes: Pasture alternate: land and grazing animals, not a named shepherd. Does not supply a literal olive grove.

artworks.title: Moonlit Landscape
artworks.tags: Asphodel Meadow; Mistbound Crossing; moonlight; river; shadows; landscape
artworks.cropNotes: An atmospheric counterpart to the dim shore and meadows of the dead. It is not an illustration of actual asphodel flowers.

artworks.title: Arcadian Landscape with resting Shepherds and Animals
artworks.tags: Laurel Grounds; Olive Pasture; Arcadia; open ground; pastoral landscape; monument
artworks.cropNotes: Use open ground, trees and the old monument as a setting for a locale. Not a literal stadium or a depiction of the Phaeacian contest.

removeLimits.16: Seven mana for a temporary opposing-power reduction is a genuine mana sink, not a self-refunding engine.
removeLimits.65: Each additional flight/combat-draw activation costs six mana and still requires connecting; no mana or untap is generated.
removeLimits.98: Rare fight support may reward each actual fight; the fight must be separately generated and the creature must survive.
removeLimits.110: A temporary +1/+1 reward can support multiple legitimate graveyard/exile arrivals; it produces no reusable resource.
removeLimits.124: Multiple instances of menace are redundant. Repeating this trigger cannot accumulate extra menace.
removeLimits.128: Three mana per +1/+1 pump is a deliberately inefficient repeatable mana sink; deathtouch itself does not stack.
removeLimits.148: A life-only death reward can trigger for each death; it does not draw, drain opponents or refund a sacrifice.
removeLimits.166: A six-mana creature can earn one counter for each arrival from exile; its trigger neither draws nor enables the next arrival.
removeLimits.176: The trigger already says for the first time each turn. Remove only the duplicate trailing clause; retain the actual first-event limit.
removeLimits.185: Six mana for double strike on this turn's crew is expensive and double strike does not stack.
removeLimits.213: The activation still costs three mana and tapping, targets another permanent, and returns it at the next end step; it cannot immediately self-loop.
removeLimits.226: Surveilling once per attack event is sufficient. The one-or-more wording already prevents triggering separately for every attacker.
removeLimits.248: Surveilling once per attack event is sufficient; additional combats can legitimately trigger it again.
removeLimits.274: The small temporary boost can reward each scry event without producing mana, cards or an untap loop.
removeLimits.299: A seven-mana rare can reward each other attacking legend with scry. It requires a real attacking board rather than a self-refunding action.

retainedLimitPolicy: Keep card-flow, mana/untap, token-production, repeatable graveyard/exile recursion and high-impact theft/lockdown restrictions unless a separately reviewed redesign removes the risk. Tapping or sorcery speed alone is not proof of safety. First-event and second-spell thresholds are not blanket-deleted.

lateSlotPolicy.unseenDeviceFlags: Do not infer a shared cut list from a different browser. Read and export the actual local review queue.

deferredLimits.146: Shared authoring row 147 is partially cleared, including its rules cell. Preserve the published rule and do not restore or infer discarded authoring values.
